topPRs.title: feat(kona): integrate kona-sp1 into the monorepo
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Closes #18489 and closes #18457.

## Summary

Adds the experimental **kona-sp1** integration — zkVM-based fault proofs for OP Stack state transitions, built on [SP1](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1) — under `rust/kona/sp1/`.

> ⚠️ **Experimental.** Establishes the crate structure and host/guest baseline. Not wired into production proving; not for production use.

## Provenance

Derived from [OP-Succinct](https://github.com/succinctlabs/op-succinct) via the standalone op-rs/kona prototype at https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051 (SP1 v5.2.2). That PR was cut from an older op-succinct (≈ v3.3.5); this PR re-aligns the host/client crates to current op-succinct, then adapts everything to the monorepo and SP1 v6.2.4.

## Scope

Ports only the **proving core**: op-succinct's `utils/{client,host,build,ethereum}` and the `range`/`aggregation` guest programs. Excludes op-succinct's `validity`, `fault-proof`, `contracts`, `bindings`, `scripts`, `signer`, and `proof` subsystems, and the host modules `block_range`, `l1_selection`, `proof_cache`, `rpc_types`, `witness_cache`. Benchmarking tooling lands separately.

## Changes vs https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051

Source is structurally inherited (same `kona-sp1-*` crates and layout). On top of it:

- **SP1 v5.2.2 (`inphi/sp1` fork) → v6.2.4 (official crates.io)**; drives the EVM/precompile API updates and ELF changes below.
- **Re-aligned host/client crates to current op-succinct** (the op-rs PR predated these): the GHSA-5jh4-3p33-85xc target-downgrade postcondition, `OpPrecompiles::new_with_spec` precompile construction, SafeDB JSON-RPC error classification, rollup-config caching/validation, KZG `Ok(false)` rejection, the network-prover builder, and panic-elimination.
- **Collapsed the range ELF variants** (`range-elf-bump` + `range-elf-embedded`) into a single `range-elf` (embedded-allocator feature removed in SP1 v6.2.4).
- **Isolated guest crypto patches** into a nested workspace; gitignored generated ELFs.
- Monorepo wiring: workspace members/deps, `deny.toml`, CI protobuf install, `just build-sp1`.

## Changes vs upstream op-succinct

At the **logic level the host/client crates track current op-succinct** (per the re-alignment above). The remaining differences:

**Structure / layout:**
- Crates renamed `op-succinct-*` → `kona-sp1-*`; `utils/` → `crates/`, Kona module layout.
- **Ethereum DA only** — Celestia, EigenDA, and AltDA range programs and their `utils/{celestia,eigenda,altda}` crates are not ported.
- `range/ethereum` + `range/utils` merged into one `range` crate.
- Added Kona-layer crates with no upstream equivalent: `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof`.

**Toolchain:**
- **SP1 v6.2.4** vs op-succinct's **v6.1.0** — pulls in a newer revm/op-revm/alloy-op-evm precompile API (`PrecompileHalt` vs `PrecompileError`, `OpTx`/`OpEvmContext` types, the gas-`reservoir` arg, fluent `Context::mainnet()…build` builder, `report.gas()`).
- A single `range-elf` (no bump/embedded variants).

**Monorepo integration:**
- Guest crypto patches **isolated in a nested `programs/Cargo.toml` workspace** (own `Cargo.lock` + `[patch.crates-io]` for sha2/sha3/crypto-bigint/k256/p256/substrate-bn), so they don't touch the monorepo `rust/` graph (upstream keeps them at its repo root).
- Generated ELFs **gitignored**; `crates/elfs/build.rs` writes empty placeholders when absent, and real ELFs build on demand via `just build-elfs`.
- Host crates wired into the monorepo `rust/` workspace.

**Monorepo-API adaptations** (newer kona/alloy than op-succinct ships):
- `is_interop_active(block_info.timestamp)` (op-succinct passes `number`).
- Blob lookups take `&[B256]` (not `&[IndexedBlobHash]`); extra `None` arg on `OraclePipeline::new`.
- `PostExecEvmFactoryHooks`/`PostExecEvmFactoryAdapter` from the monorepo's `alloy-op-evm`.
- Host-args wiring (`l2_chain_id` populated, `DataFormat::Directory`).

**Port-specific behavior:**
- A **zero-step / trace-extension short-circuit** in the witness executor: when the claimed L2 block equals the agreed safe head there is nothing to derive, so it asserts `claimed_output_root == agreed_output_root` and returns early. Lifted verbatim from kona's native client (`rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs`) so the SP1 client handles the same dispute-game edge case; op-succinct only guards `claimed < safe_head`.

**Unchanged:** the guest commitment scheme matches op-succinct (range commits `BootInfoStruct` via `sp1_zkvm::io::commit`; aggregation digests via `bincode::serialize`).

## File mapping (op-succinct → this PR)

| op-succinct | this PR (`rust/kona/sp1/`) |
|---|---|
| `utils/client` (`op-succinct-client-utils`) | `crates/client` (`kona-sp1-client-utils`) |
| `utils/host` (`op-succinct-host-utils`) | `crates/host` (`kona-sp1-host-utils`) |
| `utils/build` (`op-succinct-build-utils`) | `crates/build` (`kona-sp1-build-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/client` | `crates/ethereum/client` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-client-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/host` | `crates/ethereum/host` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-host-utils`) |
| `programs/range/ethereum` + `programs/range/utils` | `programs/range` (merged) |
| `programs/aggregation` | `programs/aggregation` |
| — (no upstream equivalent) | `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof` |

`crates/client/src/{boot,client,types,oracle/*,precompiles/*,witness/*}` and `crates/host/src/{constants,contract,fetcher,host,logger,metrics,network,proof,stats,witness_generation/*}` map 1:1 to op-succinct's `utils/client/src` and `utils/host/src`.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- Only the **guest programs** (range, aggregation) are included — no host-side programs; the host crates are libraries only.
- Monorepo CI does not yet install the SP1 toolchain or run the Dockerized ELF build, Codecov wiring, or no-std checks for the SP1 crates (#18326).
- We'll likely want to **rename the crates** once this is made more independent from SP1 and supports different zkVMs.
- Benchmarking harness lands separately.
- It's possible the roundtrip serialization of proof/public values between the range proof and agg proof do not match exactly due to `bincode` weirdness. This can be fixed in a follow-up PR if needed (requires generating two real, full range proofs and aggregating them in one agg proof); this PR chose to minimize changes from upstream op-succinct instead.

topPRs.title: fix: fail fast on cold-start backfill errors
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This is a narrow follow-up to PR #20823. It keeps the cold-start retry behavior while the supernode is waiting for VNs/SafeDB to become ready, but treats failures from the actual configured log-backfill range as fatal.

## Rationale

Once every chain has produced a SafeDB first entry, the supernode has selected the startup handoff and has begun fetching historical logs. If that historical range cannot be served, retrying the same range forever does not make progress and contradicts the intended hard-fail behavior for unavailable backfill history.

## Changes

- Wrap `runColdStartBackfill` failures in a sentinel `errColdStartBackfill`.
- Let `waitForColdStartInit` return that sentinel instead of retrying indefinitely.
- Add a unit test proving `Start` exits when the backfill range cannot be fetched after SafeDB readiness.

## Validation

- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop`
- `git diff --check`

topPRs.title: Fix supernode startup handoff coverage
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fix supernode cold-start handoff when interop activation is historical but local SafeDBs only contain recent entries.

- Treat pre-activation timestamps as inactive and distinguish post-activation timestamps that are below this node's startup handoff window.
- Gate `superroot_atTimestamp` so timestamps below the startup handoff do not query optimistic SafeDB history this node cannot have.
- For pre-activation cold start, choose the newest local-safe boundary across chains, then wait until every chain can serve that timestamp through SafeDB before sealing logs.
- Seal the recent log window ending at that SafeDB-covered handoff without pausing/restarting VNs; restarting can reset SafeDB past the selected handoff.
- Halt immediately if SafeDB history is already unavailable before any logs are sealed.

## Testing

- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot -count=1`
- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot -count=1`
- `./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot`
- `git diff --check`

topPRs.title: op-reth: generate superchain-configs.tar via build.rs, decommit it
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The op-reth side of the SR coupling (follow-up to #21474, now merged — this PR is **rebased onto develop**). It **ports op-reth's superchain-config archive generation from bash to a Rust `build.rs`** and **decommits the 9MB binary `superchain-configs.tar`** — only its `.sha256` is committed now.

- **`build.rs`** replaces `res/fetch_superchain_config.sh`, reading the `superchain-registry` submodule with pinned, deterministic crates: `toml`/`serde_json` (TOML→JSON), `zstd` (decode the dictionary-compressed genesis), `miniz_oxide` (re-emit plain zlib the `no_std` runtime inflates). Entries are sorted and tar headers fixed, so the archive is **byte-reproducible** across machines/tool versions (unlike the old `yq`/`qpdf` pipeline).
- **Semantics mirror kona's `KONA_SYNC_SUPERCHAIN`**, with one addition since op-reth's tar is gitignored (not committed text): env **unset** → use the provided `res/tar` as-is (no submodule), regenerating from the submodule only if it's **absent**; **`OP_RETH_SYNC_SUPERCHAIN=1`** (run by `just sync-superchain-rust`) → always regenerate the tar, `.sha256`, and `chain_specs.rs`. (Both env vars accept `1` or `true`.) The build.rs is **git-free** (resolves the submodule by relative path), so it works without a `.git` dir (Docker).
- The genesis `config: null` is stripped (would fail `Genesis` deserialization; the runtime re-derives it from metadata).

## Providing `res/tar` to builds (no persist infra)

The hybrid build.rs means each context just needs **either** `res/tar` **or** the submodule:
- **CI**: `rust-prepare-and-restore-cache` inits the `superchain-registry` submodule **by default** (`init_superchain_submodule: true`) — most rust jobs build op-reth's chainspec, which runs the build.rs regenerate path — so building jobs produce `res/tar` on demand. Only the no-build lint jobs (`fmt`/`typos`/`deny`/`zepter`/`no-std`) opt out with `false` (the SR shallow clone is ~4 MB). A new **`op-reth-superchain-snapshot-check`** job regenerates + diffs the committed `.sha256` + `chain_specs.rs` (catches submodule-vs-pin drift), wired into the required gate. The old prep-superchain tar-commit check is removed.
- **Docker**: the op-reth bake context is `rust/` (excludes the submodule), so a docker-bake **named context** exposes `superchain-registry` and `DockerfileOp` COPYs the `superchain/` subdir the build.rs reads to `/superchain-registry`; the in-container build.rs regenerates `res/tar`. The factory docker workflow checks out `submodules: recursive`, so the named context is populated.

## Test plan

- `OP_RETH_SYNC_SUPERCHAIN=1` refresh generates `res/tar` + `.sha256` + `chain_specs.rs`; **deterministic** across repeated runs.
- Default build with `res/tar` present uses it in ~1.5s (no submodule); with it **absent**, regenerates from the submodule and asserts the result matches the committed `.sha256`, leaving committed files untouched.
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-chainspec --features superchain-configs` — **32 passed** in all paths; `clippy -D warnings`, `zepter run check`, and `rustfmt` clean. `kona-registry` regenerates identically with `KONA_SYNC_SUPERCHAIN=1`.
- Vendored workspaces op-rbuilder + rollup-boost path-depend on the chainspec crate and keep their own `Cargo.lock`; both updated for the new build-deps.
- Rebased onto #21397 (which now loads OP Mainnet/Sepolia from the SR archive and dropped the op/base skip): build.rs drops its own op/base skip, so `chain_specs.rs` now lists `op` (Base is naturally excluded — no genesis in the SR), and the chain set is identical to develop (only the entry order differs).

Closes #21467.

topPRs.title: refactor(alloy-op-evm): Phase 0 — externalize the SDM refund inspector seam
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
## Summary

**Phase 0** of the SDM → optimism-premium extraction: introduce a refund-inspector seam in the monorepo so *which* `PostExecRefundInspector` runs becomes a construction-time choice, while keeping behavior byte-for-byte identical. **Stacked on #21502** (pre-work); review the diff against that branch.

This is the riskiest consensus-adjacent refactor in the plan — it ships **zero behavior change** and is proven so by the full workspace suite + two independent reviews.

### What changed
- **New seam** (`alloy-op-evm/src/post_exec/refund.rs`): `PostExecRefundInspector` (CTX-free; `Snapshot`, `begin_tx`, `note_account_touch`, `finish_tx -> u64`, `snapshot`, `restore`) + `NoopRefundInspector`. `SDMWarmingInspector` implements it.
- **Generic `R`**: `PostExecCompositeInspector<I>` → `<I, R = SDMWarmingInspector>`; `OpEvm` gains a trailing `R = SDMWarmingInspector` param, driven through the trait. `OpEvmFactory` stays non-generic (uses the default), so every monorepo node still installs `SDMWarmingInspector` exactly as before.
- **`finish_tx -> u64`** is the cross-repo contract. Producer warming-**attribution telemetry** (`WarmingRefundEvent`/`warming_events_by_tx`, `PostExecAdjustment.warming_events`, the post-exec-replay `refund_breakdown`) is dropped — non-consensus; it moves to premium in Phase 1.
- Executor tests that asserted intrinsic-warmth/fee-vault exclusion via attribution were re-pointed at the consensus-visible aggregate refund.
- **§6.1 CREATE-address staleness investigated → not a bug**: revm's `CreateInputs::created_address` memoizes the canonical (pre-bump-nonce) address before the inspector hook runs, so the inspector's nonce is ignored. Added a regression guard + clarifying comments.

### Plan deviation (important)
The plan's §2.1 mechanism ("collapse to the single `I` slot, no new type param") **does not compile** against alloy-evm 0.36: `BlockExecutorFactory::Executor<DB,I>: BlockExecutor for all I` forces `OpEvm<DB,I>: PostExecEvm` for *every* inspector, which is exactly why an always-present refund inspector (the composite) is required. Hence the factory-fixed `R` type param. A factory *generic* over `R` hits an HRTB-over-`DB` wall, so premium will ship its own factory fixing its `R`.

### Deferred to Phase 1
Associated-`Snapshot` opacity (kept the `Snapshot = WarmingState` bound) and the Noop-for-non-producers split.

## Testing
- Full workspace unit suite: **2527 passed**, 11 skipped.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets` clean; clippy clean on the changed crates; no-std OK.
- Producer→verifier roundtrip + settlement/receipt/state-root parity all green.
- Two independent reviews (security + adversarial correctness): **APPROVE** — consensus surface provably unchanged; dropped data is telemetry only.

## Follow-ups (tracked, not in this PR)
- §6.2: decide the `gas_refund_entries` length/DA cap (block-validity).
- Phase 1: move `SDMWarmingInspector` to premium, flip default `R` to Noop, lift the `Snapshot=WarmingState` bound to an associated `Snapshot`.
